solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A lute Elvis played on screen

indicators.note: the letters are played about with, like notes rearranged

explanation.surface: Elvis strums a lute in one of his films.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical picture makes 'played' look like strumming, and 'on screen' like a film setting, when it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Televisual describes what appears on a television screen.

clue.text: Greasy head of slippery child

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a kiddy is a small child

explanation.surface: A slippery child is covered in grease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slippery' sits so well beside 'Greasy' that it reads as more definition; only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a road that makes tyres skid is slick with grease or ice.

clue.text: Genius‘s supporter getting emails here?

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting garment
the inbox is where emails arrive

explanation.surface: A genius's backer is being sent lots of emails.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay. 'Supporter' suggests a patron, not underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainbox is informal British for a very clever person.

clue.text: Dog that’s mine short of tracks

blocks.note: a colliery is a coal mine
RY = railway, a common abbreviation; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A dog belonging to me has gone off the path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' reads as a possessive, not a pit. Take RY from COLLIERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Border and rough breeds are dogs bred for herding sheep.

clue.text: Peerage upset with new colour

blocks.note: N = new, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: The aristocracy is upset by a new colour, perhaps on a coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The peerage is the British nobility; its seven letters plus N make the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a light yellowish green like fresh peas is one colour among many.

clue.text: Soar having clipped the first wing

indicators.note: the first letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A bird tries to soar with a clipped wing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a bird with a clipped wing, so 'wing' looks like part of the scene, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb can be a wing or branch of a building or organisation.

clue.text: Wave of foam has run inside cup

blocks.note: a beaker is a drinking cup
R = run, from cricket scoring; goes inside

explanation.surface: Foam from a drink spills over and runs down the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: The foam suggests a frothy drink, but it is the sea's foam.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: a large wave that curls over and bursts into white foam on the shore.

clue.text: Caress and stroke US glam rock band

blocks.note: Kiss, the face-painted American rock band

explanation.surface: A fan caresses and strokes a member of a US glam rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caress and stroke' look like two synonyms; stroke is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A butterfly kiss is a caress made by fluttering the eyelashes against someone's skin.

clue.text: First chance

blocks.note: first as in the first night of a show or the first move in chess
a chance or opportunity, as in a gap in the market

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two meanings; 'First' is adjectival as in the opening day.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening means first in order and also an opportunity.

clue.text: Protest action for all Greeks, I learnt, misguided

indicators.note: the letters are led astray into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone learns that Greek workers staged a wrong-headed mass protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For all' is part of the definition: it is what makes the strike general.
explanation.definitionFit: A general strike is a stoppage by workers across all industries.

clue.text: Everyday routine ending in disappointment, study works

indicators.note: take the letter at the end

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it
a mill is a factory, or works

explanation.surface: A daily grind that ends in disappointment, though studying pays off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' reads as a verb, but it is a noun meaning a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the machine you walk on without getting anywhere stands for a dull daily routine.

clue.text: Good, a good French country

explanation.surface: A French country described as good twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' belongs to the wordplay, not the country: Gabon is in Africa, though French-speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a country in west-central Africa.

clue.text: School closed if yard’s fenced off

indicators.note: the answer is penned in by the surrounding letters

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of closed, through if, into the start of yard's

explanation.surface: A school shuts because its yard has been fenced off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is a verb here, meaning to teach, so the swap works: to school someone is to edify them.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct or improve someone, as to school them.

clue.text: Shriek in alarm, perhaps? One may have hives

blocks.note: a beeper is one kind of alarm
eek! is a shriek; goes inside

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks in alarm, then learns they have come out in hives.
explanation.walkthrough: Hives is also a skin rash, which is why shrieking in alarm seems natural; here they are beehives.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: the hives are beehives, and whoever tends them has them.

clue.text: Men’s clothing accessory, something fabricated that needs no introduction

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: pork pie = lie, in rhyming slang (usually shortened to porky)

explanation.surface: A fashion accessory so well known it needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang pairs a phrase with a word it rhymes with: pork pie, or porky, means a lie. 'Needs no introduction' sounds like praise but cuts the T from THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pork-pie hat is a flat-topped men's hat with a round crown.

clue.text: Throw dummy on floor, initially

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' means placed after

blocks.note: a lummox is a clumsy, stupid person

explanation.surface: Someone flings a ventriloquist's dummy to the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' looks like a physical toss, but it means to confuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to disconcert them, which is what flummox means.

clue.text: Poor woman OK about dismissal, finally steps back?

indicators.note: the letters are in poor order

explanation.surface: A poor woman, fine about being fired, finally backs away.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: the moonwalk is a dance whose steps glide backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The moonwalk, made famous by Michael Jackson, is a dance move that seems to step forward while sliding back.

clue.text: Party mischief maker ultimately lost power

indicators.note: 'ultimately' points at the final letter and 'lost' says it goes missing

explanation.surface: A political party's troublemaker has lost power in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' seems to modify 'lost power', but it tells you to drop the last letter of TROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having the upper hand over something is having power over it.

clue.text: Real company on centre ground

explanation.surface: A genuine firm is occupying the political centre ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre ground' reads as a political phrase, but 'ground' is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete means real and tangible, not abstract.

clue.text: Shout now if ordering fish

explanation.surface: A diner shouts at a waiter to order fish right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordering' fits a restaurant, but it rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this tuna, named for its yellow fins, is one kind of fish.

clue.text: Set off wearing cooler tie

indicators.note: a plan gone off has gone wrong

explanation.surface: Someone sets off wearing a trendier tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' is a device, the fan, not 'more fashionable'; 'tie' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to tie a knot or a lace is to secure it.

clue.text: Popular place for advice

explanation.surface: A well-liked place to go and get advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' reads as a noun here, but it is the verb put.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: opinions contributed to a project count as advice.

clue.text: Blank design or embroidery’s framed

indicators.note: the answer is held within the frame of the surrounding words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of design, through or, into the start of embroidery's

explanation.surface: A plain design, or someone's embroidery, hangs framed on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blank' looks like an adjective describing the design, but it is a verb: to blank someone is to ignore them.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang sense: to blank someone is to snub them by acting as if they are not there.

clue.text: Relative on Sunset Boulevard, say, wife

blocks.note: Sunset Boulevard is a street in LA, so being on it is being IN LA

explanation.surface: A relative, perhaps a wife, lives on Sunset Boulevard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Sunset Boulevard as an example of somewhere in LA.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a relative by marriage, such as a spouse's mother.

clue.text: O sugar!

blocks.note: O is shaped like a zero, and nil in tennis scoring has its own word
sugar is a term of endearment, like darling

explanation.surface: A mild curse: O sugar!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sugar!' reads as a polite swear word; it is a pet name, like love.
explanation.definitionFit: Love means nil in tennis, and is a term of endearment like sugar.

clue.text: See the setter by mostly calm wildlife sanctuary

indicators.note: most of the word, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: to get a point is to see it
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A visitor is told to see the setter beside a quiet nature reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' suggests visiting, but it means understand, as in 'I get it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a national park in Tanzania famous for its wildlife.

clue.text: Spanish article is back in Spanish city

indicators.note: the whole run of letters goes backwards

blocks.note: to be is to live, exist

explanation.surface: A Spanish news article has returned to a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: ELLIVES turned around gives SEVILLE. 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Andalusian capital, home of flamenco, is one city in Spain.

clue.text: About right, a treat roughly chopped and served raw

indicators.note: the letters are arranged only roughly

explanation.surface: A kitchen treat is roughly chopped and served raw, about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped' looks like the anagram signal but belongs to the definition, which describes steak tartare.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartare describes meat or fish finely chopped and served raw.
